今天的主题：大脑、阅读和语言学习。这组词是雅思高频话题：阅读和听力 Part 4 的科普讲座最爱讲大脑研究，常见 structure、activate、alter、fundamental 这类词；大作文常考「孩子该不该从小学双语」「电子屏幕是否让人不再读书」；口语 Part 1 和 Part 3 问 reading 时也能直接用。今天是第 5 周最后一天，每个词后面 ≈ 是同义替换，背的时候连同义词一起记。

例句

  • Children who grow up bilingual often find it easier to learn a third language.（从小说双语的孩子往往更容易学第三门语言。）
  • Learning to read alters the structure of the brain.（学会阅读会改变大脑的结构。）
  • Reading is fundamental to success at school.（阅读对在校取得好成绩至关重要。）
  • As cities grow, traffic inevitably gets worse.（随着城市扩张，交通不可避免地变得更糟。）
  • The library has a room dedicated to children's books.（图书馆有一间专门放儿童读物的屋子。）

同义替换小抄（听力最常见的考法）：

题目写 change → 录音可能说 alter　|　题目写 basic / essential → 录音说 fundamental　|　题目写 detailed / complex → 录音说 intricate　|　题目写 unavoidably → 录音说 inevitably　|　题目写 switch on / trigger → 录音说 activate　|　题目写 stand for → 录音说 represent

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，并能说出至少 15 个词的一个同义替换。再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 bilingual、ability、fundamental 写一句「从小学外语很重要」，大作文能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：How reading shapes your brain（阅读如何塑造你的大脑），5 月 14 日这一期。Becca 和 Georgie 聊阅读为什么不是天生的：大脑没有专门的「阅读区」，学阅读要借用视觉、听觉、语言等区域；读中文和读英文用到的大脑区域还不一样，有位中英双语的人中风后不能读中文却还能读英文。这集只有 6 分钟多，两段专家采访最难。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。节目后面照样有一组我按雅思格式出的题（选择 Q1–3 + 笔记填空 Q4–9）。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，像考试一样做下面的 Q1–9，只听一遍，听完点「对答案」。选择题注意：录音里先提到的说法常常是干扰项，要听到最后的结论。
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Rebecca Gotlieb 那段语速快、术语多（auditory、cortex、lobes），先读懂中文再听。
  4. 第三遍挑 Georgie 讲双语男子那段（"Scientists studied a bilingual man..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：natural（天生的）、dedicated（专用的）、co-opt（征用，拉进来）、circuit（回路）、inevitably（不可避免地）、intricate（复杂精细的）。

Questions 1–9（按雅思格式自编）

Questions 1–3　Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

1 When does Georgie usually read?
A on her way to work　B before going to bed　C at lunchtime

2 According to Maryanne Wolf, reading is
A as natural as speaking.　B not natural at all.　C easier to learn than speaking.

3 After his stroke, the bilingual man
A could no longer read English.　B could not read either language.　C could still read English but not Chinese.

Questions 4–9　Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

Reading and the brain

• At birth, the brain has networks for seeing and making sounds, but not the 4 needed to read

• Evolution has not given us a 5 reading brain

• Reading activates all four 6 of the cortex

• Reading Chinese needs more visual 7 and visual processing

• Proust's novel contains about 8 words

• One sentence in it has more than 9 words

答案：1 B　2 B　3 C　4 pathways　5 dedicated　6 lobes　7 memory　8 1.3 million　9 900。同义替换提示：题目 before going to bed = 录音 before bed；题目 not natural at all = 录音 It isn't natural at all（这题是原词，但 A 选项 as natural as speaking 是录音前面 Becca 说的「误导项」）；题目 Evolution has not given us = 录音 our brain hasn't had enough time to develop；题目 more than 900 = 录音 over 900。

点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Becca：Hello. Welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Becca.

Becca：大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是贝卡。

Georgie：And I'm Georgie. Remember, you can find all this episode's vocabulary along with a transcript and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com. Now, Becca, do you read a lot?

Georgie：我是乔治。别忘了，这一期的所有词汇、文稿和练习题都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。贝卡，你平时读书多吗？

Becca：Hmm, I don't read often. I just feel like I don't have the time, Georgie. How about yourself?

Becca：嗯，我不常读书，总觉得没时间。你呢，乔治？

Georgie：I would love to read more, but I don't read very much at the moment. I read mostly before bed because I feel like it helps me relax放松 and go to sleep. And today we're talking all about reading. We'll be hearing from some experts专家 about how reading can change our brains, and as usual we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.

Georgie：我很想多读点，但现在读得不多。我主要在睡前读，因为感觉读书能帮我放松、入睡。今天我们就来聊聊阅读。我们会听几位专家讲讲阅读怎样改变我们的大脑，照例也会学一些有用的新单词和短语。

Becca：Let's start with a quiz question. The longest novel长篇小说 in the world is widely thought普遍认为 to be by French author作者，作家 Marcel Proust, a book which, when translated翻译 into English, means Remembrance of Things Past《追忆似水年华》（普鲁斯特的小说）. But how many words does the book contain包含? Is it:
a) 130,000,
b) 1.3 million, or
c) 13 million?

Becca：先来一道小测验。人们普遍认为世界上最长的小说出自法国作家马塞尔·普鲁斯特之手，这本书译成英文叫《追忆似水年华》。那么这本书有多少个词呢？是 a) 13 万，b) 130 万，还是 c) 1300 万？

Georgie：OK. The longest novel长篇小说 in the world. I still think 13 million words sounds too many, so I'm going to go with选择，决定要
b) 1.3 million.

Georgie：好，世界上最长的小说。我还是觉得 1300 万个词太多了，所以我选 b) 130 万。

Becca：Alright. We'll find out at the end of the programme节目结尾. Now, we might think of reading as like speaking. We're born with天生具有 the potential潜力，潜能 to do it and then we learn. It's natural. If something is natural, it's something you were born with天生具有 or that comes from nature.

Becca：好的，节目最后揭晓答案。我们可能会觉得阅读和说话一样：生来就有这个潜力，然后慢慢学会，是天生的（natural）。natural 指的是你与生俱来的，或者来自大自然的东西。

Georgie：But Maryanne Wolf, author作者，作家 of the book Reader Come Home, says that this isn't true.

Georgie：但《Reader Come Home》（《回家吧，读者》）一书的作者玛丽安·沃尔夫说，事实并非如此。

Maryanne Wolf：We think of language as natural, and reading is written language so it must be natural. But it isn't. It isn't natural at all.

Maryanne Wolf：我们认为语言是天生的，而阅读是书面语言，所以阅读肯定也是天生的。但不是这样，阅读根本不是天生的。

Becca：Scientific studies suggest that when we're born, our brains already have the networks that allow our eyes to see and our vocal cords声带 to produce sounds, but not with the pathways通路，途径 we need to read.

Becca：科学研究表明，我们出生时，大脑已经有了让眼睛看东西、让声带发出声音的网络，但没有阅读所需要的通路。

Georgie：Let's hear more from psychologist心理学家 and neuroscientist神经科学家 Rebecca Gotlieb, speaking to the BBC World Service.

Georgie：我们再听听心理学家、神经科学家丽贝卡·戈特利布接受 BBC 国际台采访时怎么说。

Rebecca Gotlieb：From an evolutionary进化的 timescale, our brain hasn't had enough time to develop a dedicated专用的，专门的 reading brain. And so, to build a reading brain network, we co-opt征用，（硬）拉进来 parts of the brain involved in vision视觉，视力 and auditory听觉的 processing, and language, and attention and affect情感，情绪（心理学用词）. Reading is really a whole brain process. It involves activation激活 in all four lobes（大脑的）叶 of the cortex大脑皮层. The process of developing a reading brain alters改变 everything, from brain activity to brain structure结构 and brain connectivity连接性，连通. The power of deep reading深度阅读 is really fundamental根本的，至关重要的 to our humanity人性，作为人的本质. When we read deeply, we change our brains and we change who we are.

Rebecca Gotlieb：从进化的时间尺度来看，我们的大脑还没有足够的时间发展出一个专门用来阅读的大脑。所以，为了搭建阅读的大脑网络，我们征用了大脑里负责视觉、听觉处理、语言、注意力和情绪的部分。阅读其实是整个大脑都参与的过程，大脑皮层的四个脑叶全都会被激活。形成「阅读脑」的过程会改变一切，从大脑活动到大脑结构，再到大脑各部分之间的连接。深度阅读的力量对我们之所以为人至关重要。当我们深度阅读时，我们改变了自己的大脑，也改变了自己是谁。

Becca：Rebecca says that our brains haven't evolved进化 to include a dedicated专用的，专门的 reading brain. Dedicated专用的，专门的 here means designed and used for one particular purpose.

Becca：丽贝卡说，我们的大脑还没有进化出专门的阅读脑。dedicated 在这里的意思是为某一个特定用途而设计和使用的。

Georgie：So, because we don't have a part of the brain designed specifically专门地 for reading, when we learn to read, we co-opt征用，（硬）拉进来 other parts of the brain. Co-opt征用，（硬）拉进来 here means to include someone or something, often against their will违背他们的意愿.

Georgie：所以，因为大脑里没有专门为阅读设计的区域，我们学阅读的时候就要征用大脑的其他部分。co-opt 在这里的意思是把某人或某物拉进来，而且常常是违背其意愿的。

Becca：Right. Learning to read means using lots of different parts of the brain that are designed for other things, and this changes our brain structure结构 compared to someone who hasn't learned to read.

Becca：没错。学阅读意味着要用到大脑里很多本来为别的事情设计的部分，这让我们的大脑结构和没学过阅读的人不一样。

Georgie：And the language we read also shapes our brain. Chinese characters（汉）字, for example, use symbols符号 instead of letters of the alphabet字母表里的字母 to represent代表，表示 words and ideas.

Georgie：而且我们读的是哪种语言，也会塑造我们的大脑。比如汉字就是用符号而不是字母来表示词语和意思。

Becca：Research suggests that learning to read these symbols符号 activates激活 different areas of the brain to reading an alphabet-based system.

Becca：研究表明，学习读这些符号激活的大脑区域，和读字母文字时不一样。

Georgie：Scientists studied a bilingual双语的 man who could read and speak Chinese and English. The man suffered a stroke中风, which affected parts of his brain, including his ability to read Chinese. But amazingly, he was still able to read English.

Georgie：科学家研究过一位会读会说中文和英文的双语男子。他中风了，大脑的一些部分受到影响，包括读中文的能力。但神奇的是，他仍然能读英文。

Becca：Maryanne Wolf explains more to the BBC World Service.

Becca：玛丽安·沃尔夫向 BBC 国际台做了进一步解释。

Maryanne Wolf：It's a beautiful example of how the brain's circuit回路，电路 reflects反映 the requirements要求，需要 of Chinese, which inevitably不可避免地 means more visual memory and visual processing of those beautifully intricate复杂精细的 symbols符号 or characters（汉）字.

Maryanne Wolf：这是一个很好的例子，说明大脑的回路反映了中文的要求：中文不可避免地需要更多的视觉记忆，以及对那些精美复杂的符号或汉字进行视觉处理。

Georgie：Maryanne says that the brain's circuit回路，电路 is shaped by learning to read Chinese. A circuit回路，电路 is a system of connections.

Georgie：玛丽安说，大脑的回路是被学读中文塑造出来的。circuit 指的是一套连接系统。

Becca：The visual qualities of Chinese symbols符号 inevitably不可避免地 mean more visual areas of the brain are developed. Inevitably不可避免地 means in a way that cannot be stopped or avoided.

Becca：汉字的视觉特点不可避免地让大脑里更多的视觉区域得到发展。inevitably 的意思是无法阻止、无法避免地。

Georgie：Maryanne describes the symbolic Chinese characters（汉）字 as beautifully intricate复杂精细的. If something is intricate复杂精细的, it has lots of detail.

Georgie：玛丽安形容这些象征性的汉字「精美复杂」（intricate）。如果某样东西 intricate，就是说它有很多细节。

Becca：And something which also has lots of detail, or certainly lots of words – I asked you, Georgie, how many words are in Marcel Proust's Remembrance of Things Past《追忆似水年华》（普鲁斯特的小说）.

Becca：说到同样有很多细节、肯定也有很多词的东西：乔治，我问过你普鲁斯特的《追忆似水年华》有多少个词。

Georgie：I said 1.3 million.

Georgie：我说 130 万。

Becca：And you were correct!

Becca：你答对了！

Georgie：Yay!

Georgie：耶！

Becca：The book also contains包含 lots of very long sentences, including one with over 900 words.

Becca：这本书里还有很多超长的句子，其中一句超过 900 个词。

Georgie：One sentence with 900 words? That is a lot. OK. It's time to recap回顾，概括 the language we learned during this programme, starting with natural, which describes something you were born with天生具有 or that comes from nature.

Georgie：一句话 900 个词？真不少。好，现在来回顾一下这期节目学到的词。先是 natural，形容与生俱来的或者来自大自然的东西。

Becca：Dedicated专用的，专门的 can describe something that is designed and used for one particular purpose.

Becca：dedicated 可以形容为某一个特定用途而设计和使用的东西。

Georgie：If you co-opt征用，（硬）拉进来 someone or something, you involve them, sometimes against their will违背他们的意愿.

Georgie：co-opt 某人或某物，就是把他们拉进来，有时是违背其意愿的。

Becca：A circuit回路，电路 is a system of connections – for example, in the brain.

Becca：circuit 是一套连接系统，比如大脑里的回路。

Georgie：Inevitably不可避免地 means in a way that cannot be stopped or avoided.

Georgie：inevitably 的意思是无法阻止、无法避免地。

Becca：And intricate复杂精细的 describes something which has lots of detail.

Becca：intricate 形容有很多细节的东西。

Georgie：That's it for this episode of 6 Minute English. Test what you've learnt with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Georgie：这一期《六分钟英语》就到这里。可以用我们网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上的练习题检测一下学到的内容。

Becca：Thanks for joining us. Goodbye!

Becca：谢谢收听，再见！

Georgie：Bye.

Georgie：拜拜。

过关标准：Q1–9 答对 7 题以上；不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（为什么阅读不是天生的、学阅读怎样改变大脑、读中文和读英文有什么不同）；Georgie 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. This room is ______ to quiet study; no phones allowed.（专用的）
  2. If you don't sleep enough, you will ______ feel tired the next day.（不可避免地）
  3. The carpet has an ______ pattern of flowers and birds.（复杂精细的）
  4. Learning a new skill can ______ the way your brain works.（改变）
  5. In maths, the letter π ______ a number close to 3.14.（代表）
  6. Good communication is ______ to a happy relationship.（根本的）
点开看答案

开头那题选 b，130 万个词，Georgie 猜对了。书里最长的一句超过 900 个词。填空：1. dedicated 2. inevitably 3. intricate 4. alter 5. represents 6. fundamental

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 1 / Part 3 做准备）：Do you prefer reading paper books or reading on a screen? Why? 用英语说两三句：I prefer ... because ... / For example, ...。也可以想想：你学英语的时候，感觉大脑和读中文时有什么不一样？
